text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The High Court today found Kota Melaka Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng guilty of false publication and sedition and fined him 15,000 ringgit, putting him in danger of losing his parliamentary seat.
-- The government will not come to the aid of Sukom Ninety Eight Bhd, the organiser of the Kuala Lumpur Commonwealth Games in 1998, if it incurred losses from staging the event from Sept 11 to 21.

-- Buyers of the Kancil compact car and Rusa van need to wait only for about two months now to get their vehicles compared to four months previously, auto assembler Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd said.

-- Major trading countries are now trying to link trade with politics after failing to link it with labour, human rights and environment issues, International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz said.

-- From July, payment for and delivery of shares will have to be made within five days of the transaction, Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange president Salleh Majid says. At present, delivery is T plus five and payment T plus seven.
